_: Material regions for FullDoomguyclassic-single-notex.glb.
This asset carries NO material information: one glTF material with a flat
grey baseColorFactor of 0.604, no texture, no image, no COLOR_0, POSITION
and NORMAL only, and one connected component after welding. So unlike the
diorama -- whose three materials were measured out of its texture -- these
regions are AUTHORED. They are a statement about the model, not a
measurement of it, and they are in this file rather than inside a
heuristic so that they can be argued with.
Coordinates are the importer's normalized space at --height 19 --up z:
Z up with the base at 0, XY centred on the bounding box. The model
measures x -6.64..6.67, y -6.01..6.01, z 0.01..19.00, and the regions
below were read off that.
The figure, by height band: rocky base 0..2.5, boots 2.2..5.2, legs to 9,
torso 9..16, helmet 16..19. The gun is the only part that is hopeless to
bound with an axis-aligned anything -- it is held across the body and runs
diagonally out to (3.1, -5.3, 9.3) -- which is what the capsule is for.

families.name: armour
_: The hue the diorama's dominant material measured at, so the two
statues share one palette design. Nothing about this asset chose it;
there was nothing here to choose with.

families.name: kit
_: Helmet, gun and boots. Near-neutral and slightly warm, because the
only material statement the file actually makes is a neutral grey,
and because a hard-kit material reading as a second saturated hue
would compete with the armour instead of sitting under it.
-0.12 in Oklab L is the albedo offset, a little under one ramp step
(0.125 at the current band). Enough that the kit is unmistakably a
darker material at the same incident angle, not so much that its own
five stops stop describing its shape.
